text: Use a separate printed hinge pin through the aligned bores, with an axial retainer and enough plastic surrounding the bores to resist tearing.
Keep the hinge extension local to the middle that needs it and preserve a strong, supported pivot.
Align a single smooth, continuous, convex contact with the actual OP1 switch at its working angle. Make it wide enough for reliable clicks without precise hand alignment or a dip that can catch.
Keep the DFRobot paddle snug in the hinge with minimal side, angular and fore-and-aft play. It must click and return with its keeper installed, including when pressed near the middle at an angle.

Seat the DFRobot touch board with its white connector facing down and its flat touch face exposed. Keep both mounting holes aligned, clips strong enough for fitting, and plugged wiring clear below the board.
Place the pivot toward the upper end of the paddle to give the lower-row click adequate leverage. Preserve the fitted hardware and assembly clearances.
Keep the paddle centred on the mouse click, prevent side-to-side tipping or loss of the pivot and reinforce the hinge-arm roots against breakage.
Avoid exposed protrusions at the paddle end that merely limit travel or get in the way of the click.
An earlier hinge used flexible paddle arms that snapped into holes in the carrier. The later pin hinge replaced that attachment.
The former snap-in hinge arms were too narrowly spaced to reach both pivot seats. The complaint concerned span, not pin diameter.
Increase the spring friction of the centre clip only if testing shows that it works loose. The fitted reference clip held in handling.
R57’s pin and centre clip held during handling, and the sliding retainer held down the board. The paddle could catch under a downward pull with the retainer in place.
The assembled R58 clicked better and wobbled less. Broken loose material could jam the click. Once fully seated, the board posts and their clips fitted correctly.
R63 initially felt improved. Later handling found renewed wobble where the DFRobot holder enters the hinge. A previous fitted revision was snug.
The early snap-hinge trial had weak outer arms, debris around the hinge and lateral tipping during the click.

Keep less than 10 mm between the top edge of the DFRobot board and the hinge, returning toward the compact earlier design with only the extra clearance needed for the actual mated connector and right-side wire exit throughout click travel. Avoid pinching the conductors.

Lower the slide-in keeper arm so it retains the OP1 board without blocking paddle travel at the centre or far end. Check balanced retention on both sides, full click and return, and easy keeper insertion. Adjust the downward actuator only as needed for clearance.
Remove the exposed flat pointed or triangular projection behind the hinge. Keep the connector-down touch board and compact right-side wire exit without an unnecessary projecting platform.

The printed R68 click was less reliable with the final keeper installed, especially with force near the paddle end. The underside-view right-hand retention appeared weaker; the precise contact causing interference remains to be established.
